name: Bn Advance: Adv Gd, one Coy vanguard
note: A Bn group as the Advance Guard of a Bde's advance, in single column (MIB p 83 para 23 a: the vanguard normally a Coy group; IBB S33 para 3 p 138). The click is the SP the vanguard's head crosses; the aim is the direction of advance. The vanguard a rifle Coy with a Sec of the Bn mortars, an assault pioneer Sec, the ATGM Pl, tanks if allotted and the FOO (IBB p 138; MIB p 82 e: tanks always in the vanguard, by day and night); Bn HQ one bound behind the rear troops of the vanguard (MIB p 81 b); the Mor Pl and the ATGM well forward (MIB p 82 g, h); the main guard behind. Laid on IBB Fig 12 p 150 (the night formation, the only one IBB draws): the vanguard 500-600 m deep, link groups 800-900 m (40-65 min) to the main guard, which by night moves at least 300-400 m behind the vanguard (p 149; IC s64 para 6 c p 280: not less than 400-450 m, which the Main Gd row holds to by night). Fig 12 is judged by night only. By day the gaps are reckoned in time, not space (IBB p 138 para 4; IC s61 para 6 p 261), and in open country with good visibility the leading Coy may be strung on the road up to 1100-1400 m and the Bn over 3-5 km (IC s61 para 7 p 261): the day Vanguard and Bn spread rows. The axis band 1.6 km wide: by day the Bn clears at least 800 m either side of the axis in open country (IBB p 133). With the terrain the axis is routed for tracks, its water crossings read, bounds laid on the water ahead (IC s58 para 4 p 242), report lines on the lateral roads and railways (para 6 p 243) and halting areas sited on the ground short of the bounds (IBB p 160); who leads, tanks or infantry, read from the country (MIB p 82 f).
